gbm_population_evidence.quote: SUBSTUDY 1: Diagnosis of recurrent glioblastoma and intention to treat with bevacizumab

candidate_evidence.quote: II. Determine the efficacy, as measured by the 4-month progression free survival (PFS) rate, of propranolol and imipramine, when used in combination with bevacizumab for the treatment of recurrent glioblastoma. (Subprotocol 1: PRIME)

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: NOTE: Patient may be enrolled following completion of surgery and/or radiation therapy for newly diagnosed or recurrent tumor.
SUBSTUDY 1: Diagnosis of recurrent glioblastoma and intention to treat with bevacizumab

role_evidence.quote: GROUP A: Patients receive propranolol orally (PO) twice daily (BID) and standard of care (SOC) bevacizumab intravenously (IV) every 3 weeks of each cycle.
GROUP B: Patients receive imipramine PO once daily (QD) and SOC bevacizumab IV every 3 weeks of each cycle.
Patients with recurrent glioblastoma receiving bevacizumab on the GHoST Master Protocol as assigned by their treating physician are randomized to 1 of 2 groups.

agents.drug_class_hint: anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody, standard of care for recurrent GBM

role_evidence.quote: Patients also receive standard of care chemotherapy as assigned by their treating physician as part of the platform on study.

agents.drug_class_hint: physician-assigned standard-of-care systemic chemotherapy for glioma (unnamed; lomustine mentioned in outcomes)

coder_notes: Master protocol (digital remote-monitoring platform, any glioma, SOC chemotherapy, registry phase NA) plus randomised Subprotocol 1 (PRIME) in recurrent GBM: propranolol + SOC bevacizumab vs imipramine + SOC bevacizumab. Each subprotocol arm has one investigational agent -> experimental_monotherapy; neither arm is a control. Registry data error: Group A arm lists 'Drug: Imipramine' and not bevacizumab among its interventions; arm/description text shows Group A receives propranolol + bevacizumab, so arms assigned per text. treatment_setting 'both' because master protocol enrols newly diagnosed or recurrent glioma; the candidate substudy is recurrent GBM only. No antitumour mechanism stated for propranolol or imipramine.
